patch_description: This program is a crossover of two prior ANSATZ designs combining the best ideas: symmetry-grouped single-qubit rotations, compact parameter sharing, and explicit winning-line three-qubit motifs. The evolved ansatz reduces the number of distinct parameters per block to 13 (matching the stronger candidate) while keeping expressive three-body ZZZ and CCRZ motifs aligned with the tic-tac-toe win lines. Two-qubit couplings use shared CRZ parameters (outer ring vs. center spokes) rather than many unparameterized CZ/CNOT gates, lowering parameter count and encouraging trainable entanglement. Symmetry-based sharing (corners/edges/center) regularizes and improves parameter efficiency. The block intentionally reuses parameter keys (no extra parameters for post-phase flexibility), aligning expressive power with parameter efficiency to improve validation/test accuracy and reduce train-test gap compared to the current program.
